case_metadata.case_name: Sasikala Pushpa v. State of Tamil Nadu
laws_referred: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 - S.438, S.340
Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act, 1998 - S.4
Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 - S.9(I)(n), S.10, S.16, S.17
Tamil Nadu Public Property (Prevention of Damage and Loss) Act, 1992 - S.3

judge.name: Justice R. Banumathi
judge.role: Presiding Judge, Supreme Court of India
judge.remarks: Authored the unanimous judgment. Emphasized the expediency requirement under Section 340 CrPC and the absence of mens rea.

judge_2.name: Justice S. Abdul Nazeer
judge_2.remarks: Concurred fully with Justice Banumathi's judgment.

defense_counsel.name: Mr. Sanjay Hegde
arguments: The date on the vakalatnama was a clerical error.
High Court failed to record expediency under Section 340 CrPC.

prosecution_counsel.name: Mr. Yogesh Kanna
prosecution_counsel.role: Counsel for State of Tamil Nadu
arguments: First appellant did not sign in Madurai.
This is a fraud upon the court.

appellant_1.name: Sasikala Pushpa
appellant_1.remarks: Former MP. Explained she signed in New Delhi on 16.08.2016.

appellant_3.name: Husband of Sasikala Pushpa
appellant_3.remarks: Businessman. Explained he delivered the vakalatnama to Madurai.

advocate_vijaykumar.name: Mr. S. Vijaykumar
advocate_vijaykumar.remarks: Attested the vakalatnama in good faith.

procedural_history.event: Delhi High Court granted interim protection to appellants in Crime No. 5/2016.
Appellant No.1 and son signed vakalatnama in New Delhi.
Appellant No.1 left for Singapore. Appellant No.3 delivered vakalatnama to advocate in Madurai.
Appellants filed anticipatory bail with vakalatnama showing Madurai date.
POCSO charges added in Crime No. 5/2016.
High Court directed appellants to explain discrepancy.
Appellants filed affidavit stating clerical error.
Madras High Court dismissed bail and directed complaint for forgery.
High Court granted bail to Appellants 2 & 3 in Crime No. 276/2016, denied to Appellant 1.
Supreme Court granted interim protection to Appellant 1 in Crime No. 276/2016.

key_legal_issues.issue: Whether High Court was justified in directing criminal complaint for forgery based on mistaken date.
key_legal_issues.finding: No. The mistake was inadvertent and did not amount to fraud or forgery.

key_legal_issues.issue: Whether High Court complied with Section 340 CrPC expediency requirement.
key_legal_issues.finding: No. High Court failed to record such a finding.

key_legal_issues.issue: Whether appellants had mens rea for forgery.
key_legal_issues.finding: No. Signatures were admitted. No wrongful gain or loss.

final_judgment_and_orders.order: Appeal allowed. FIR and charge sheet quashed.
Interim protection extended. Anticipatory bail granted. Liberty to approach High Court for quashing.

legal_principles_established: Before prosecution under Section 340 CrPC, court must record satisfaction that it is 'expedient in the interest of justice'.
Expediency is judged by impact on administration of justice, not injury to individual.
Incorrect statement in vakalatnama does not automatically constitute fraud or forgery.
Mens rea is essential for forgery.
Vakalatnama is procedural; its date does not affect merits.

simulation_conversation.speaker: Judge Banumathi
simulation_conversation.dialogue: Mr. Hegde, please begin your arguments for the appellants.

simulation_conversation.speaker: Defense Counsel
simulation_conversation.dialogue: My Lord, the date on the vakalatnama was a clerical error. The appellants have admitted their signatures.

simulation_conversation.speaker: Judge Banumathi
simulation_conversation.dialogue: Mr. Kanna, what is the State's response?

simulation_conversation.speaker: Prosecution Counsel
simulation_conversation.dialogue: My Lord, the first appellant was in Singapore. She never came to Madurai. This is fraud.

simulation_conversation.speaker: Judge Banumathi
simulation_conversation.dialogue: But the signatures are admitted. Where is the forgery?

simulation_conversation.speaker: Prosecution Counsel
simulation_conversation.dialogue: My Lord, the document states it was signed in Madurai. That is false.

simulation_conversation.speaker: Judge Banumathi
simulation_conversation.dialogue: Mr. Hegde, what about the requirement of Section 340 CrPC?

simulation_conversation.speaker: Defense Counsel
simulation_conversation.dialogue: My Lord, the High Court did not record that it was expedient in the interest of justice.

simulation_conversation.speaker: Judge Nazeer
simulation_conversation.dialogue: Was any finding recorded regarding expediency?

simulation_conversation.speaker: Defense Counsel
simulation_conversation.dialogue: No, My Lord. The High Court jumped to the conclusion of fraud.

simulation_conversation.speaker: Prosecution Counsel
simulation_conversation.dialogue: My Lord, fraud on the court vitiates everything. This Court held so in Sachida Nand Singh.

simulation_conversation.speaker: Judge Banumathi
simulation_conversation.dialogue: But what is the impact on administration of justice? It is a procedural document.

simulation_conversation.speaker: Prosecution Counsel
simulation_conversation.dialogue: My Lord, a false document filed in court is itself an impact.

simulation_conversation.speaker: Judge Banumathi
simulation_conversation.dialogue: Mr. Hegde, explain the sequence of events.

simulation_conversation.speaker: Defense Counsel
simulation_conversation.dialogue: My Lord, Appellant No.1 signed in Delhi on 16th. Appellant No.3 took it to Madurai on 17th.

simulation_conversation.speaker: Judge Nazeer
simulation_conversation.dialogue: And the date on the vakalatnama?

simulation_conversation.speaker: Defense Counsel
simulation_conversation.dialogue: Mistakenly recorded as 17th at Madurai. It should have been 16th at Delhi.

simulation_conversation.speaker: Prosecution Counsel
simulation_conversation.dialogue: My Lord, the handwriting expert has given a report. The signatures may not be genuine.

simulation_conversation.speaker: Defense Counsel
simulation_conversation.dialogue: My Lord, the appellants have admitted their signatures. Expert opinion cannot override that.

simulation_conversation.speaker: Judge Banumathi
simulation_conversation.dialogue: Ms. Sasikala, do you have anything to say?

simulation_conversation.speaker: Appellant 1
simulation_conversation.dialogue: My Lord, I never intended to commit fraud. It was a mistake. I am deeply sorry.

simulation_conversation.speaker: Judge Banumathi
simulation_conversation.dialogue: Mr. Vijaykumar, you attested the vakalatnama. What do you say?

simulation_conversation.speaker: Advocate Vijaykumar
simulation_conversation.dialogue: My Lord, I acted in good faith. I received the document from Appellant No.3.

simulation_conversation.speaker: Judge Nazeer
simulation_conversation.dialogue: Was the date mentioned by you?

simulation_conversation.speaker: Advocate Vijaykumar
simulation_conversation.dialogue: No, My Lord. The date was pre-filled. I verified the signatures only.

simulation_conversation.speaker: Judge Banumathi
simulation_conversation.dialogue: Ms. Banumathi, you are the complainant. What is your view?

simulation_conversation.speaker: Witness Banumathi
simulation_conversation.dialogue: My Lord, these people have harassed me. They are capable of anything.

simulation_conversation.speaker: Judge Banumathi
simulation_conversation.dialogue: But do you have personal knowledge of the vakalatnama?

simulation_conversation.speaker: Witness Banumathi
simulation_conversation.dialogue: No, My Lord. But they are liars and cheats.

simulation_conversation.speaker: Judge Banumathi
simulation_conversation.dialogue: Inspector, what did your investigation reveal?

simulation_conversation.speaker: Investigating Officer
simulation_conversation.dialogue: My Lord, we filed chargesheet based on the High Court's direction.

simulation_conversation.speaker: Judge Banumathi
simulation_conversation.dialogue: Did you find any evidence of wrongful gain?

simulation_conversation.speaker: Investigating Officer
simulation_conversation.dialogue: No, My Lord. But the false statement is itself an offence.

simulation_conversation.speaker: Judge Banumathi
simulation_conversation.dialogue: This Court has considered all submissions. The appellants have admitted their signatures. The incorrect date is a clerical error. There is no mens rea. The High Court failed to record expediency under Section 340.

simulation_conversation.speaker: Judge Nazeer
simulation_conversation.dialogue: I agree. The power under Section 340 cannot be used casually. The impact on administration of justice is minimal here.

simulation_conversation.speaker: Judge Banumathi
simulation_conversation.dialogue: The appeal is allowed. FIR and charge sheet in Crime No. 1331/2016 are quashed.

simulation_conversation.speaker: Judge Nazeer
simulation_conversation.dialogue: What about the other cases?

simulation_conversation.speaker: Judge Banumathi
simulation_conversation.dialogue: Interim protection in Crime No. 5/2016 and Crime No. 276/2016 is extended till disposal.

simulation_conversation.speaker: Judge Banumathi
simulation_conversation.dialogue: Appellants are granted anticipatory bail in Crime No. 276/2016. They may approach High Court for quashing.

simulation_conversation.speaker: Judge Banumathi
simulation_conversation.dialogue: The appellants shall not resort to any consequential proceedings based on this quashing.

simulation_conversation.speaker: Judge Banumathi
simulation_conversation.dialogue: With these observations, all appeals are disposed of. Court stands adjourned.
